decisions.decision: What is Voicebox and how does it work? Summarize the architecture and performance.
decisions.answer: Voicebox is a large-scale, text-guided multilingual speech generation system built as a non-autoregressive continuous normalizing flow (CNF) model trained with flow-matching to infill missing speech conditioned on surrounding audio and text. Architecturally, it uses a 24-layer Transformer audio model with convolutional positional embeddings and ALiBi bias, 16 attention heads, 1024-dimensional embeddings, 4096-dimensional feed-forward layers, about 330M parameters, and UNet-style skip connections between symmetric layers, plus a separate 8–10-layer duration model (512-dimensional embeddings, 2048-dimensional FFN, 28M–34M parameters) that decouples timing from acoustics for finer alignment control.[8630634a96d2c217][95f87546ff2baac9] As a non-autoregressive flow-matching model, it differs from standard autoregressive TTS systems by transforming noise into speech through a small number of flow steps rather than predicting frames sequentially; this allows it to condition on both past and future context, which is particularly useful for editing or generating segments in the middle of an utterance.[a8ca5e9c5c7e89c][95f87546ff2baac9] The number of flow steps (or function evaluations) at inference can be adjusted to trade off quality against latency, and high-quality speech can be produced with fewer than ten non-autoregressive steps, whereas VALL-E requires one autoregressive and seven non-autoregressive stages.[95f87546ff2baac9][7607c9f8b2af6566] Voicebox operates on Mel-spectrogram features with a HiFi-GAN vocoder, a choice motivated by comparisons against alternatives such as Parallel WaveGAN and Encodec-based features.[4e9476e69e8394de] It is trained on more than 50K hours of speech that are explicitly described as neither filtered nor enhanced, giving it exposure to diverse noise, emotion, and acoustic conditions.[806cea72b0cda9b8] In terms of performance, Voicebox supports mono- and cross-lingual zero-shot TTS, speech inpainting, content editing, style conversion, denoising, and diverse sampling via in-context learning, and can generate speech up to 20 times faster than the best autoregressive models.[806cea72b0cda9b8][a2ae4512e4877e2d] On English zero-shot TTS, it outperforms VALL-E on intelligibility and similarity, achieving a word error rate of 1.9% versus VALL-E’s 5.9% and a similarity score of 0.681 versus 0.580, while maintaining these speed advantages.[806cea72b0cda9b8][a2ae4512e4877e2d] It also shows strong style transfer and infilling performance, surpassing baselines such as A3T and Demucs on text-guided denoising and speech infilling in terms of WER, similarity, and mean opinion score.[524382862327c52c][95f87546ff2baac9]
decisions.notes: Addresses architecture (Transformer CNF, duration model, vocoder), training data scale and noisiness, non-autoregressive flow-matching vs autoregressive models, and performance including WER 1.9% vs 5.9% and speedups. However, it does not explicitly reference an 'In-filling' or 'Flow Matching' diagram; the only figures cited are Figure 1 (task generalization) and Figure 2 (NFE trade-off), so the specific requirement to ground mid-sequence generation in those diagrams is not fully met.
